title: First incompleteness: Gödel sentences and Rosser's theorem

based_on.title: An Introduction to Gödel's Theorems, second edition, corrected Logic Matters reprint

summary: Construct arithmetic sentences that a consistent, effectively axiomatized extension of Robinson arithmetic can neither prove nor refute.
abstract: Checking a proposed proof is a finite task, but that does not mean an arithmetic theory can settle every arithmetic question. We turn the proof checker into a formula and construct a sentence saying that it has no proof. Consistency rules out a proof of this Gödel sentence; ruling out its negation takes a stronger hypothesis in the original argument. Rosser changes the sentence to compare proofs of opposite conclusions and obtains an undecided sentence from consistency alone. The result applies to every effectively axiomatized extension of Robinson arithmetic. A separate argument shows that even without effective axioms, a consistent extension cannot have a total recursive test for its theorems.
